An $a \times b$ cell loop is the boundary of an $a \times b$ rectangle, and its interior is an $(a-2) \times (b-2)$ rectangle. If we have 5 loops that partition the $10 \times 10$ grid, their bounding boxes must form a laminar family (a tree of rectangles) where the outermost rectangles perfectly tile the $10 \times 10$ grid, and each non-leaf rectangle's interior is perfectly tiled by its children.

If the roots are all leaves (i.e., $m$ roots), they must all be $2 \times k$ or $k \times 2$ rectangles. If there is only 1 root, it must have $m-1$ children which tile its $(x-2) \times (y-2)$ interior. This gives the recurrence relation:
$$P(m, x, y) = P(m-1, x-2, y-2) + \sum_{\text{tilings of } x \times y \text{ by } k \text{ rectangles}} \sum_{\substack{m_1+\dots+m_k = m \\ m_i \ge 1}} \prod_{i=1}^k P(m_i, x_i, y_i)$$
